races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Princess Honey Bee
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who has finished placed twice on Standard AW going including a win at 6f, and Craig Lidster's filly should control every yard of this mile from the off with no pace rival to challenge her lead.

runners_data.name: All Shall Be Well
runners_data.note: Deeply lightly-raced and running style entirely unknown, Jason Watson takes the ride for Jack Jones whose yard is in decent nick at 2/15 over 14 days; her OR of 120 is conspicuously high for this grade and her ceiling relative to rivals is the most significant wildcard in the race.

runners_data.name: Barbuda Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who wears a hood and has course experience on Standard AW going, but her form string of -86053 reveals a horse who has struggled to convert proximity into victories; Roger Teal's runner will need a stronger pace than Princess Honey Bee is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Mystic Music
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up filly placed in her most recent outing at 8f on Good ground and has shown she handles Standard AW, but her 0-from-3 record and lack of a prominent early position leaves her reliant on a fast pace that this small field is unlikely to generate.

runners_data.name: Hamdania
runners_data.note: Won her only start over 7f on Standard AW and now returns after 271 days off, a significant fitness question mark for any horse, yet James Horton's 2/11 14-day record and the booking of George Wood suggest connections are confident she arrives ready to run a full race; her prominent style makes her the natural danger to the leader.

races.paceDynamic: Princess Honey Bee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and will stride to the lead from the off on the Lingfield AW mile, setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo with no rival capable of pushing her early. Hamdania, who showed prominent tendencies on her sole start, may track her from second, but the genuine pace pressure simply will not materialise in this small field. Barbuda Bay and Mystic Music will settle in behind in their customary hold-up roles, while All Shall Be Well's style is unknown and unlikely to disrupt the controlled shape. With a lone leader dictating a measured gallop on a standard surface, this race shape strongly favours front-running or close-tracking profiles — horses able to control the race from a handy position will be hardest to pass late, while deep closers will face a stiffer challenge if the tempo never truly tests the leader's stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader controls, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Honey Bee dictates an unchallenged, measured pace and her rivals cannot generate enough late momentum.
scenarios.body: Princess Honey Bee leads at her own tempo on the Standard AW surface, and with no one to force a genuine gallop the field will be strung out chasing a horse in her comfort zone; the mile on this track suits a front-runner who can quicken into the home straight rather than be ground down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hamdania, tracking closely from second, uses her winning AW experience and fresh legs after 271 days to pick off the leader entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Hamdania's sole outing was a win over 7f on Standard AW going and she races off a long absence with James Horton sending her out fit enough to run a big race; sitting a length off the leader throughout, she would be ideally placed to collar Princess Honey Bee inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closers swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a fast-finishing run for the hold-up horses over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mystic Music has placed on this surface at this trip and Barbuda Bay has course experience, meaning both could pick up ground if Princess Honey Bee goes too hard early; however, the expectation of a controlled pace makes this scenario structurally unlikely in a five-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown factor lands
scenarios.trigger: If All Shall Be Well, lightly raced and unquantified, produces a performance that belies her unknown style profile and outclasses this modest field.
scenarios.body: With an OR of 120 she carries a significant rating advantage on paper and Jason Watson is booked for what could be a well-treated debutante type with a ceiling well above her rivals; if she possesses natural speed or class to overcome positional uncertainty, she could win with any style.

watchPoints.text: Princess Honey Bee leads uncontested — if she bowls along at a comfortable clip through the first half-mile, she could prove very difficult to reel in on this flat Standard surface with only four pursuers.

Hamdania returns after 271 days off; watch the paddock and early market moves closely — if she is backward in coat or condition, her chance of tracking the pace effectively throughout a mile is compromised.

All Shall Be Well's OR of 120 stands out against rivals rated 60-68 — if that rating reflects genuine class rather than a lightly-raced quirk, she could potentially win from almost any position regardless of pace shape.

Barbuda Bay wears a hood and has a tendency to finish midfield without threatening — in a slowly-run race behind a lone leader, she is unlikely to generate the late momentum needed to win unless the pace collapses entirely.

Mystic Music's best AW run came over 8f at Goodwood; on this course, with a controlled gallop, Nicola Currie will need to find an alternative route past rivals if the leader is not stopping — watch for positional moves rounding the home turn.

races.name: Castle Air Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: Won over 11f on Standard AW eight days ago in good form, and the step back to 1m4f is a slight query on whether the trip fully stretches this hold-up type; Olivia Haines claims 7lb and Jim Boyle's yard is running at only 1/13 over 14 days, so support signals are muted.|

runners_data.name: Romantic Spirit
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter dropped 68 days off a run and David Menuisier has sent out zero winners from 16 runners in the past fortnight, which are notable negatives; however, Saffie Osborne takes the ride and on Standard AW across 13 of the last 15 runs this horse has an outstanding record of finding the front, meaning the tactical advantage of uncontested lead is real regardless of trainer form.|

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Standard AW and placed at 13f, giving it the most relevant trip-and-surface profile in the field; however, Gary and Josh Moore's runner is a genuine hold-up type placed in midfield on this map because the back of the field is already occupied — it will race closer to the pace than ideal, which tempers confidence in its ability to reproduce a trademark closing effort over 41 days off.|

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Carries a hood and has won on Standard AW at 12f, giving Marcus Tregoning's four-year-old solid course credentials; a prominent style and the ability to track a single front-runner economically makes this a natural beneficiary of the dominant race shape, and Marco Ghiani's experience of the track is a positive for timing a challenge from second or third.|

runners_data.name: Wiltshire Wonder
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who won over 12f on Standard AW but has been off 82 days and has shown inconsistent form in recent outings, including a 10th over the same course-and-distance; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim reduces the weight burden, but the hold-up style and long absence make this an each-way outsider dependent on a pace scenario that is unlikely to materialise.|

races.paceDynamic: Romantic Spirit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead, should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f Lingfield AW trip. Twilight Moon and Sibling Rivalry will press prominently behind, but neither is a natural leader and both are more likely to track than challenge Romantic Spirit for the rail position in the early stages. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the back — Mister Daydream, nominally a hold-up horse, is mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is effectively occupied, meaning it will race somewhat out of its natural role. With one horse controlling a steady, uncontested pace on a Standard surface, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-pace profiles that can track the leader conservatively and pounce in the straight, rather than true closers relying on a truly-run gallop to generate momentum from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Romantic Spirit Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Spirit leads unchallenged and sets a controlled tempo, allowing prominent trackers to race handily.
scenarios.body: Romantic Spirit sets a comfortable lead and the race unfolds at a measured pace, with Twilight Moon and Sibling Rivalry tracking within striking distance before the final bend; the prominent stalkers who conserve energy in second and third are best positioned to collar the leader late or run on strongly. This shape rewards the P-style runners who can sit just off a slow-to-moderate gallop and time their challenge in the home straight.)

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Spirit's controlled pace is slow enough that it retains enough in reserve to repel all challengers in the straight.
scenarios.body: Romantic Spirit exploits the lack of early pressure to dictate every fraction, arriving at the two-furlong pole full of running and proving too strong for any hold-up horse to reel in; the prominent trackers cannot quite get past a leader that has simply had too easy a time of it. This is the scenario where a front-runner on Standard AW ground with course experience and clear control converts the race into a procession.)

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Charge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely slow and the field bunches, freeing Big Bear Hug or Wiltshire Wonder to produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A crawl in the early stages compresses the field entering the straight, and the hold-up runners get a clear run on the outside to produce late momentum that overwhelms a tiring leader; Big Bear Hug's win at this sort of trip on Standard and Wiltshire Wonder's previous course form give them slim but real claims. This scenario is discounted because Mister Daydream — the most likely beneficiary — is racing out of its true role and the rear of the field is not occupied by genuine hold-up types in position to generate the required closing burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble Decides
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses entirely mid-race causing a tactical reshuffle with Mister Daydream and Big Bear Hug threading through from central positions.
scenarios.body: A false or stop-start gallop creates a bunched, muddling scenario through the back straight, and horses mapped centrally — including Mister Daydream, who is not racing from its natural hold-up position — find themselves with a clear passage as the prominent runners fade; the winner emerges from an unlikely source in the middle of the pack. This shape is assigned low probability because it requires both a genuine pace collapse and hold-up horses who are not truly settled at the back to produce a finishing effort from an unfamiliar position.

watchPoints.text: Watch Romantic Spirit's jumping away — any slow start removes its only meaningful advantage and immediately hands tactical control to Twilight Moon or Sibling Rivalry, reshaping the entire race.

Monitor Twilight Moon's hood in the preliminaries; if it shows signs of freshness or early keenness it could overshoot its natural prominent position and become embroiled in a duel with Romantic Spirit that benefits neither.

Mister Daydream's drawn position and early movement will indicate whether Jason Watson attempts to push forward toward midfield from the outset or is forced even further back — a horse racing well out of its natural role could be the most significant non-finisher in a race that otherwise falls to a tracker.

Big Bear Hug, fresh off a win eight days ago, is worth watching early to see if the short turnaround leaves it sluggish out of the stalls — a clean break is essential for a hold-up type that needs to make ground from the rear in a potentially slow-run race.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forager
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a win at Lingfield AW on Standard last month but is a genuine hold-up horse whose best efforts come from off the pace; redistributed into midfield here simply because the field is unusually rear-heavy, meaning Jack Mitchell may find this race shape slightly awkward to navigate from a slightly more forward position than ideal, and the 0/2 trainer strike rate over 14 days adds a mild caution.

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Back-to-back five-furlong Lingfield AW wins on Standard give him an excellent course and distance profile; Jason Watson's booking is a positive, and with three wins and six places from 15 runs on similar going, the draw and flat track suit a horse whose natural hold-up style can be deployed cleanly without redistribution pressure in a small field.

runners_data.name: Diomed Duke
runners_data.note: The sole pace-maker here, and his ability to lead uncontested is the defining tactical fact of this race; his AW course form shows just one win from 15 runs on Standard, and a tongue-tie is fitted, but those concerns are partially offset by Olivia Haines' 7lb claim reducing his burden and the fact that no rival is equipped to push him off the front.

runners_data.name: Truly Glamorous
runners_data.note: Won twice in quick succession on Good ground and has form figures of 1-1-4-6 on 5f recently, suggesting she retains ability; her natural closing style has been mapped into midfield because the field is saturated with hold-up types, so Gina Mangan will need to ride tactically against the horse's instincts, and the 35-day absence without a trainer 14-day strike rate is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Noble Vow
runners_data.note: Two of his five career wins have come on Firm and Soft, and his Standard AW record shows 0 wins from 10 runs, which is a meaningful concern on today's surface; his OR of 80 tops the field, but Alec Voikhansky's booking and a 35-day break alongside that poor AW going record temper any confidence in him translating natural hold-up ability into a winning run here.

runners_data.name: Toolatetonegotiate
runners_data.note: Three wins and seven places from 15 runs on similar going make his profile look solid on paper, and a headgear change to a hood (hg:p) may sharpen his early focus; however, his true running style is hold-up and he has been placed into midfield by redistribution, so Millie Wonnacott (5lb claim) will face a tactical challenge fitting a natural closer into a shape where genuine closers already outnumber available rear positions.

races.paceDynamic: Diomed Duke is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner sprint and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead from the gates, he can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo over Lingfield's straight five furlongs on Standard ground. Wyle Cop and Noble Vow sit at the rear as genuine hold-up types who will need the pace to set them up, while Forager, Toolatetonegotiate, and Truly Glamorous are natural hold-up or prominent racers who have been redistributed into the midfield map position because the field carries more closers than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear. With Diomed Duke able to roll along comfortably in front without being pressured, the tempo is unlikely to be severe enough to open the race wide for deep finishers, and the profile that benefits most clearly is the hold-up runner who can track just off the pace in a compressed midfield and produce a sharp, well-timed finish — not the pure, last-to-first closer who needs genuine pace to run at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diomed Duke Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Diomed Duke leads from the break and sets a comfortable, metronomic gallop that is never genuinely challenged by any rival.
scenarios.body: Diomed Duke dictates every yard of the five furlongs without burning energy fighting for position, arriving at the two-furlong pole well within himself and able to extend when the race quickens; horses who track him closely in second or third position benefit from the slipstream before unleashing a short, punchy finish on a flat, straight track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Him In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Diomed Duke's moderate pace unexpectedly quickens too sharply in the final two furlongs, leaving a gap for riders who have conserved energy off the back of the field to close.
scenarios.body: Wyle Cop or Noble Vow, racing from their natural hold-up positions, benefit if the pace is just genuine enough to create a meaningful gap at the furlong pole; the straight Lingfield track with its consistent Standard surface rewards a straight, uncomplicated finishing run without swerving into trouble.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Trio Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Forager, Toolatetonegotiate, and Truly Glamorous into midfield accidentally produces an unpredictably high early tempo as those horses jockey for prominent positions.
scenarios.body: A busier early pace would string the field out and suit a horse with tactical versatility who can slot just behind the leader and sustain their effort, but because all three redistributed horses are racing out of their natural role their ability to produce their best is genuinely compromised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Diomed Duke, who has limited course-and-distance form on the All-Weather and is tongue-tied, overcooks the early fractions alone in front and ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A complete leader collapse would gift the race to the deepest closers, but this remains the least likely scenario given the uncontested nature of the lead and the Standard conditions that impose no undue physical stress on the pace-setter.

watchPoints.text: Diomed Duke's early fractions are the race's central variable — if he is allowed to idle in front unchallenged, the race could be run at a misleadingly slow tempo that renders deep hold-up horses like Noble Vow and Forager unable to generate the momentum they need.

Wyle Cop's back-to-back five-furlong Standard wins at Lingfield make him the horse most likely to exploit a compressed midfield finish; watch whether Jason Watson positions him to track the leader directly rather than being shuffled to the rear in a small field.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Forager, Toolatetonegotiate, and Truly Glamorous — racing slightly against their natural instincts creates a risk of a muddled, slow-motion early stride pattern if any of their riders attempt to push forward earlier than planned.
Noble Vow's AW going record (0 wins from 10 runs on Standard) is worth monitoring in betting markets; his OR advantage over rivals could be misleading if his best form is genuinely surface-dependent.

Truly Glamorous has won twice in her last four starts but both victories came on Good ground; her 35-day absence and the Standard AW surface combine to make a smooth return harder to predict, and her jockey Gina Mangan has limited opportunities to find rhythm on a horse racing out of its natural position.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 / EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Kss De Triomphe Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lost In Wonder
runners_data.note: Consistent AW performer on Standard going (3/5 similar-going runs placed or better) but 122 days off is a significant concern, and the return over 10f and 8f trips last season suggests this 2m trip requires stamina she hasn't confirmed; Tom Queally adds experience but the layoff is the overriding question.

runners_data.name: Further Measure
runners_data.note: Strong AW staying form (2W3P in 14-15 similar-going runs) and this 9-year-old knows the trip thoroughly, but Marco Ghiani is deputising for a hold-up horse now set to lead, a role that inverts its natural style and makes STYLE_FIT 0.80 a genuine concern — the pace it sets will define the entire race shape.

runners_data.name: Charles Morin
runners_data.note: Landed a win over 12f on Standard 16 days ago and Pat Phelan's yard shows 0/1 in the last 14 days, but the blinkers headgear and the form reversal (1st last time after a run of 11ths and 6ths) demands respect; a true hold-up type that the map places in midfield, meaning it may need to push forward slightly against its grain.

runners_data.name: Ada Rose
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy sends this 3yo out 30 days fresh with Jack Mitchell in the plate — a yard firing at 5/20 in 14 days — and the filly's sole Standard-going win came over 12f, 4 furlongs shorter than today's trip; a natural rear-of-field runner compressed into midfield on the map, so whether she gets her true rhythm over this marathon trip is the key question.

runners_data.name: Fabled Spirit
runners_data.note: Archie Watson yard in decent form (5/23 T14) and the horse's most relevant recent run is a 2nd over 2m on Standard just 26 days ago, making it the only runner with a near-identical prep; the fades-in-finish flag is a real worry over this trip, and as a natural hold-up type the map position overstates its likely mid-race presence.

runners_data.name: Sir Griflet
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's 3yo has been consistent in AW staying handicaps (4th over 2m on Standard last time, tp headgear) without winning, and while the 4/9 placed record on similar going shows competitiveness, a string of 0W0P finishes signals a horse that gets close but doesn't clinch — the compression of this false-pace race could suit or frustrate equally.

runners_data.name: Romeo's Guardian
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3yo steps up sharply in trip from its recent 6f runs to 2m — a massive ask — and the fades-in-finish warning combined with no wins or placed finishes (0W0P) in Standard going paints a concerning picture; blinkers headgear and the 14-day return are minor positives, but the trip jump is the dominant factor against.

races.paceDynamic: Further Measure is the only confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up style, meaning this 2m contest will be run at a controlled, sustainable tempo with no genuine front-runner forcing the pace — essentially a false-pace scenario in slow motion. With Further Measure setting a sedate gallop and the remaining six runners all being true hold-up or rear-of-field types, the race is likely to develop into a muddling, compressed affair where the field bunches through the middle stages before a sprint-style finish over the closing stages. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Ada Rose, Sir Griflet, Charles Morin, Fabled Spirit and Romeo's Guardian are all genuine off-the-pace types, yet most are shown in midfield simply because there is no room at the back; the runners most likely to actually secure prominent positions in reality are Further Measure and, to a limited extent, whichever of Ada Rose or Charles Morin is quickest from the stalls. This compressed, falsely-run staying contest over 2m on AW at Lingfield favours any runner with a sharp tactical turn of foot when the race truly ignites — those with form in muddling, slowly-run races and the ability to quicken late are most advantaged, while persistent front-runners and proven hold-up performers with a strong closing kick hold the key edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If Further Measure dictates a slow tempo unchallenged and the race ignites only in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Further Measure's uncontested lead produces a crawl through the first mile, setting up a sprint finish where tactical awareness and a sharp change of gear becomes decisive rather than stamina. Horses with proven form in muddling AW staying races and a clean late kick — particularly those with strong Standard-going handicap form — are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the field fragments in the final quarter-mile and the true closers find a clear passage to deliver runs from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo through the first 12 furlongs leaves the field tightly bunched turning in, and any hold-up horse that avoids traffic and picks up strongly in the final 2f can overhaul rivals who have gone too soon. Ada Rose and Charles Morin, despite redistribution pressures, have the Standard-going form to benefit if they find clear daylight late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Further Measure, despite racing out of natural hold-up role, maintains a brisk enough gallop to string the field out and simply outstays rivals.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role at STYLE_FIT 0.80, Further Measure would need to find a genuine front-running performance to grind rivals down over 2m at Standard, but the horse does carry strong AW staying form across 14-16f trips and the 9-year-old's experience could prove telling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Finish, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race evolves into a chaotic, compressed sprint in the last furlong with no single horse dominating and a lower-rated runner sneaks through.
scenarios.body: A completely false pace with seven hold-up horses crammed together can produce unpredictable finishes where a fresh, well-handicapped runner with course form finds a gap at rewarding odds. Fabled Spirit's recent 2nd over 2m on Standard and Sir Griflet's consistent placing form give each a slim but genuine each-way squeak.

watchPoints.text: Further Measure's opening pace will be the single most important factor in this race — if Marco Ghiani allows an overly sedate gallop, the entire field compresses and the race becomes a sprint finish that negates Further Measure's stamina edge.

Ada Rose and Charles Morin are both natural hold-up types squeezed into a midfield mapping — watch the early stages to see whether Jack Mitchell or Liam Wright push forward to claim a position or drop back to their true hold-up ground, as this will alter the effective field order dramatically.

Romeo's Guardian's trip jump from 6f to 2m is extreme and the fades-in-finish flag makes it a potential pacemarker casualty if it clips heels in a tight, bunched finish — watch for it being crowded out or stopping quickly in the final furlong.

Fabled Spirit's 2nd over 2m on Standard 26 days ago is the standout piece of specific form, but the fades-in-finish flag on a horse racing a compressed 2m finish is worth monitoring closely if it hits the front prematurely before the winning post.

races.name: Csis - Neigh Nonsense Insurance Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a sharp recent form line including a win and place over 6f on Standard going; stepping up to 7f for only the second time and that sole 7f run ended in a ninth on Soft — the trip and pace scenario here both represent a question mark.|

runners_data.name: Hamaleel
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's mare has solid course-and-distance form with ten runs at 7f on Standard going yielding a win and six places; races from hold-up, so needs a pace she can chase down, which this controlled tempo may not deliver.|

runners_data.name: Dark Brunette
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed filly for Jane Chapple-Hyam with only three career runs — her sole Standard going run was a placed effort over 6f and her running style is unclassified, making her a genuine unknown in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan takes the ride on this Mark Usher mare who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature; shuffled into a midfield position by the weight of traffic at the rear, she is unlikely to get the deep-ridden run her best form has required, and the discount on her chances in this shape is warranted.|

runners_data.name: Lili Marleen
runners_data.note: Carries a worrying recent form line of 0FP908 and is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; her true hold-up style has been pushed into a midfield mapping by the crowded rear, and the combination of fading tendency and positional compromise makes this a difficult race for her.|

runners_data.name: Espanita
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance for Charlie Johnston but has since regressed; naturally a hold-up horse who secured a prominent position on her winning day, she will be squeezed toward midfield here where the crowded field reduces her chance of replicating that effort.|

runners_data.name: Angels' Share
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly in essence whose best form has come over this 7f Standard trip with two placed efforts; the congested rear of the field means she races further forward than ideal, and the gap between her natural style and available position is the key constraint on her chance.|

runners_data.name: Daisy Roots
runners_data.note: The only genuine second-string pace horse in the race for Jim Boyle; consistent form string of 4-4-7-4-4 over this course and trip suggests she finds a level but rarely wins — tracking Ironist gives her the best tactical position in the race.|

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: George Margarson's four-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and the key pace horse in the race; the STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges her best position is not always the lead, but no other runner forces her off it here, making her likely to dictate at a pace that may suit her more than her bare figures suggest.|

runners_data.name: Cixi
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's three-year-old has placed at 7f on Standard going and is one of the more potent hold-up runners in the field based on OR; Jack Mitchell is an astute jockey for this type of tracking race and Cixi is among the best credentialled closers if the race opens up at all.|

races.paceDynamic: Ironist is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, Saffie Osborne can dictate terms at a sustainable, controlled tempo over Lingfield's 7f Polytrack layout. Daisy Roots is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Ironist into second, meaning the early sectionals are unlikely to be punishing — a pace scenario that historically rewards horses who can travel in the first three or four and unleash a finish from a position of strength rather than from deep. The closers — Cixi, Sugar Sugar, Hamaleel and Searchingtheblues — will need to make up ground against a pace that may not be severe enough to bring them into play at the business end. This race shape firmly favours hold-up-to-prominent racers who get a position no worse than midfield and can strike from there, with the controlled gallop meaning true deep closers face a difficult task. This field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the rear of the field can accommodate; Cixi and Sugar Sugar are best placed to secure a genuinely useful tracking position, while Searchingtheblues, Espanita, Angels' Share and Lili Marleen will likely find themselves shuffled wider and further back than their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ironist Controls, Closers Struggle
scenarios.trigger: If Ironist dictates a measured pace unchallenged and the field fans wide in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ironist sets a comfortable gallop with Daisy Roots tracking, and the lack of genuine pace means the race is run at a tempo that rewards those closest to the front turning in; hold-up horses face too much ground to make up against a field that does not string out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough that the front two tire in the final furlong, allowing a close-tracking runner to swoop.
scenarios.body: Daisy Roots or a horse who secures a prominent position early is ideally placed to strike as Ironist flattens, with the steady early fractions meaning energy is conserved for the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If traffic clears late and a true closer finds a gap at a crucial moment inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A sustainable pace means closers are unlikely to be delivered by natural race flow, so this scenario requires the race to fracture or a clear split to materialise; Cixi and Hamaleel are best credentialled if that happens given their course form and positive sim-going records.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Natural Order
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding, a stumble, or a significant pace injection from a rival unsettles the tempo entirely.
scenarios.body: An unexpected acceleration or incident could negate Ironist's advantage and throw the race open to any prominent runner who avoids trouble; this is the least likely shape given the clear dominance of one pace horse.

watchPoints.text: Ironist sets the pace unchallenged — if Saffie Osborne controls tempo from the front and Daisy Roots tracks snugly in second, the race may be effectively over for all hold-up horses by the home turn; watch whether any runner can close the gap in the final furlong.

Searchingtheblues, Espanita, Angels' Share and Lili Marleen are all natural hold-up horses who will be competing for the same real estate in the final two or three positions — watch for crowding and interference in the early stages as multiple horses fight for limited rear space.

Hamaleel has solid course-and-distance form but her hold-up style is a liability in a slowly-run race; watch whether Conor Whiteley opts to push her forward earlier than usual to compensate for the lack of pace.

Dark Brunette is lightly raced and her running style is unclassified — watch the early stalls break closely, as she could emerge as a surprise pace factor or alternatively drift to the rear and be swamped by the modest gallop.

Daisy Roots returns after 30 days off for Jim Boyle and has a consistent recent record over this course and trip; watch whether she tracks Ironist aggressively from the outset, as securing the position directly behind the leader is the single most valuable piece of tactical real estate in this race shape.

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: A consistent 6f performer for David O'Meara with a win over this course and distance, but by nature a hold-up horse shuffled into midfield here because the rear is overcrowded; the visor is retained and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim helps on the weights, though racing out of role softens the appeal.

runners_data.name: Bucklow Hill
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and only horse with a win on Standard AW going in his recent form; Jason Watson for Charles Hills and fresh off 42 days, he faces no pace rival to harass him and should get things entirely his own way from the front — the key horse around which every scenario pivots.

runners_data.name: Watchdog
runners_data.note: Won twice in quick succession in the summer (soft and good ground) and comes here after a 99-day absence; a true hold-up horse by inclination who will be ridden patiently by Egan, though the layoff is a genuine concern and he will need the early pace to be strong enough to deliver his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who has placed twice on Standard AW at this trip and shapes as the likely second horse into the race; Voikhansky rides and recent form has been modest, but the prominent style gives him a cleaner run than most of the hold-up pack and he sits in a tactically favourable position.

runners_data.name: Go Lockers Go
runners_data.note: A front-three finisher on AW twice recently (6f and 5f), Go Lockers Go is naturally suited to being close to the pace but finds herself mapped to midfield in a race with too many hold-up types; George Wood has a live book here and her best chance rests on the tempo being strong enough to bring her late effort into play.

runners_data.name: Far Too Fizzy
runners_data.note: Extremely course and going-familiar with 14 of her 15 career runs on Standard AW — a huge positive — and she ran just two days ago, which is the primary concern; David Loughnane's filly is a hold-up type by nature, working from midfield in this shape, and Laura Pearson will need a clear lane inside the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: George Scott's highest-rated runner in this field (OR 75) with two AW wins and a pair of seconds at 6f on Standard; Marco Ghiani rides and the horse's hold-up style is genuine, but in this race he is positioned closer than he would naturally get — a marginal advantage over the further-back hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Romeo Montague
runners_data.note: Returns after a 210-day absence for Richard Spencer, having won over this exact course and distance on Standard going; Saffie Osborne takes the mount, the layoff is a major flag to watch, but if he returns fresh and ready he has the strongest profile of the hold-up runners given his proven 6f AW win and top rating alongside Acclaimed Freedom.

races.paceDynamic: Bucklow Hill is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, he should slide into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the gates — a sustainable, controlled tempo that keeps the race together rather than stringing it out. Pilgrim's Progress is the likeliest horse to press him from a prominent berth, while the remainder of the field — Come On Over, Watchdog, Go Lockers Go, Far Too Fizzy, Acclaimed Freedom, and Romeo Montague — are all genuine hold-up types who will fill midfield and rear positions in a race that simply cannot accommodate them all at the back. The field holds more hold-up runners than the track can absorb cleanly; of those, Acclaimed Freedom and Romeo Montague are highest-rated and likely to secure the most forward of the hold-up positions, giving them a marginal tactical edge over those queuing further back. With one front-runner dictating a measured gallop at 6f on a Standard Polytrack, this race shape strongly favours a runner tracking in second or third — close enough to pounce without being drawn into a pace battle — making the prominent-to-tracked profile the single most advantaged position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bucklow Hill Controls Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Bucklow Hill secures the lead uncontested and sets a fair, metronomic gallop that rewards those closest to him.
scenarios.body: Bucklow Hill dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, and the runner tracking him in second or third — most likely Pilgrim's Progress — arrives with a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong before the hold-up pack can close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Bucklow Hill sets a fraction too fast early and a prominent-tracking runner cruises into contention turning for home.
scenarios.body: A slightly-above-sustainable early pace weakens Bucklow Hill in the final 100 yards, allowing a horse who has tracked in third with cover — likely Acclaimed Freedom or Romeo Montague — to hit the line strongly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bucklow Hill sets a genuinely strong pace that creates enough tempo for a true hold-up runner to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds at a clip fast enough to cause attrition up front, and one of the redistributed hold-up types — most plausibly Come On Over or Watchdog, both proven 6f winners — finds clear daylight late to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddling Melee
scenarios.trigger: If Bucklow Hill's uncontested lead produces an unusually slow early pace that causes a bunched finish with multiple challengers arriving simultaneously.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race in which the entire field compresses into the final two furlongs, turning the race into a sprint from the two-pole where raw sprint ability and a high draw matter most.

watchPoints.text: Bucklow Hill's early gallop speed is critical — if he is allowed to coast in front unchallenged, he becomes genuinely hard to pass and the front-runner scenario escalates significantly.

Romeo Montague has been off 210 days; if he returns rusty or under-cooked, Saffie Osborne may struggle to get competitive in what shapes as a strongly run finish, and his odds may not fully reflect the absence risk.
Far Too Fizzy ran only two days ago — watch for any sign of carry-over fatigue in her stride early, which would undermine her hold-up profile at the business end.

With five hold-up types competing for the same rear-to-midfield ground, watch for traffic in the straight — a horse who secures a clean outside run (likely Acclaimed Freedom or Watchdog) holds a significant positional advantage over those trapped on the inner.

Pilgrim's Progress has posted two placed efforts at this course and trip on Standard; if she travels smoothly behind Bucklow Hill in second, Richard Hannon's runner could be the value prominent-tracking beneficiary if the favourite ties up.

races.name: Air Ambulance Charity Kent Surrey Sussex Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Muy Muy Loco
runners_data.note: Won at this trip and course on Standard going and returns in competitive form after a recent win, but his natural hold-up style means he will be carried into midfield in a field already congested at the back; the headgear note (hg:h) is worth monitoring for any change in approach, and T14 of 1/9 for trainer Simon Dow keeps the yard angle mildly live.

runners_data.name: Haveagobeau
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with all five recent runs on Good ground and just 9/15 on similar going — the switch to Polytrack Standard is a surface query; he is a genuine hold-up horse pressed further forward by field congestion, and at OR 54 carrying 132lbs the weight is not prohibitive if the tempo enables a late swoop.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: The most interesting hold-up type in the field: wins at 12f and 8f on Standard, top trainer T14 of 2/23 for George Scott, and the 3lb claimer Liam Wright lightens the load to 131lbs; distance stepping back to 1m2f from her latest AW win at 12f may be a slight concern, but her course versatility stands out.

runners_data.name: Boston Run
runners_data.note: Prominently raced but without a win and with 0W2P on similar going (6/15 runs), his form string of 0-6642 is unencouraging; he could track The Bay Warrior but has shown a tendency to fade late, and trainer Simon Dow running two here (with Muy Muy Loco) suggests he is the second string.

runners_data.name: Celtic Spirit
runners_data.note: All five recent runs on Good ground with zero wins on similar going (0W0P, 3/8 runs), raising a legitimate surface concern on Polytrack Standard; mapped to midfield despite being a true hold-up type, the horse has struggled for consistency and the Finley Marsh booking is low-key.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Consistent record of finishing sixth across multiple course-and-distance types tells its own story — 0W0P on similar going (3/15), and Saffie Osborne's booking does not offset a form profile that has shown no spark at this level; 136lbs top weight adds further pressure.

runners_data.name: The Bay Warrior
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with an exceptional course record (14/15 runs on Standard, 1W4P) and the clearest tactical role in the race; 67 days off is the one genuine flag, and at 136lbs joint-top weight he has to carry his fitness into a race he will control in terms of tempo — his Lingfield familiarity is a significant asset.

races.paceDynamic: The Bay Warrior is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the off, he is likely to control tempo from the gates at a measured, sustainable gallop over Lingfield's 1m2f Polytrack circuit. Boston Run is the only other horse mapped prominently, and while he may track The Bay Warrior, he lacks the inclination to force the issue and is unlikely to stretch the pace. That creates a steadily-run race rather than a searching gallop, which will compress the finish and reduce the advantage of getting cover in the early stages. This shape firmly favours horses who can travel close to the pace and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the straight, rather than deep closers who need a strong early tempo to deliver their effort — making prominent and handy profiles the key beneficiaries. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Muy Muy Loco, Haveagobeau, and Celtic Spirit are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to congestion, and of those, Lady Of Clover — a confirmed hold-up type with course form and a recent win at this trip on Standard — is best-placed to get a workable position if the redistributed runners are shuffled back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bay Warrior Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If The Bay Warrior dictates an uncontested lead at steady tempo and uses his stamina advantage off a long break to repel late challengers.
scenarios.body: The Bay Warrior sets a comfortable gallop, denying rivals a true end-to-end test, and his Lingfield course affinity (14/15 runs on Standard, 1W4P) means he knows every yard; at a fair pace his fitness question (67 days off) is the only caveat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Bay Warrior goes too slow early, compressing the field and allowing genuine closers to peel wide in the straight and use superior turn-of-foot.
scenarios.body: Lady Of Clover is the most credible closer here with wins on Standard at this trip and strong jockey booking; Haveagobeau finds his best form at Goodwood but has course-proximity to work with.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Gallop Rivals Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Boston Run moves up alongside The Bay Warrior early to inject genuine pressure and the leaders empty the tank of the hold-up horses before the home straight.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely scenario given Boston Run's weak form and hold-up tendencies on his recent runs, but if he does press the pace the race becomes a true test of stamina that suits the horse who can maintain rhythm widest late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Tactical Upset
scenarios.trigger: If The Bay Warrior weakens quickly after a slow-burn leader's race and the race falls apart for a midfield stalker to exploit.
scenarios.body: Muy Muy Loco won at this course and trip on Standard (1/10f/STA) and carries the clearest form credential for this scenario, though his redistributed midfield tag means he is unlikely to be ideally positioned to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: The Bay Warrior's 67-day absence is the single biggest danger signal — if he shows any sign of greenness or fading after the home turn, the race opens up dramatically for any horse able to track him through the early stages.

Lady Of Clover drops back to 1m2f having won over 12f on Standard at this course; if the trip proves too sharp for her hold-up style she may not get competitive in time, but she is the one to watch visually making her move in the straight.

Boston Run is the key pace pressure wildcard — if Marco Ghiani elects to press The Bay Warrior rather than sit second at a distance, the tempo could spike and transform the race shape entirely from what the map suggests.

Three redistributed hold-up types (Muy Muy Loco, Haveagobeau, Celtic Spirit) will all be tracking closer than ideal; watch for congestion and potential traffic issues entering the home straight if any of them tries to switch wide simultaneously.

Saliko carries 136lbs on a 0W0P going record and six consecutive placed-at-best runs — monitor whether the top weight and going combination produce an even earlier fade than recent form suggests, which would shape the finish for the closers behind.
